claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is in an as-solidified, single-phase solid-solution state.
Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alters solute diffusivity in FeNiCrMn.
Removing Co alters dislocation kinetics in FeNiCrMn.
Dynamic strain aging becomes the dominant deformation mechanism at intermediate temperatures and moderate strain rates.
The relevant dynamic-strain-aging window is expected to occur at approximately 500–700 K.
Altered solute mobility in the absence of Co produces transient solute–dislocation pinning centers.
At intermediate temperatures, solute atoms temporarily lock mobile dislocations.
Transient solute locking of mobile dislocations produces serrated flow.
Transient solute–dislocation interactions increase strain-rate sensitivity.
Transient solute–dislocation interactions enhance strain hardening.
Enhanced strain hardening from dynamic strain aging improves the strength–ductility balance relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, the Co-free alloy will exhibit more prominent serrated flow around 500–700 K.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, the Co-free alloy will exhibit enhanced strain-rate sensitivity around 500–700 K.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, the Co-free alloy will exhibit a higher strain-hardening rate around 500–700 K.
The predicted mechanical signatures will correlate with microscopic evidence of transient dislocation pinning and solute segregation.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is expected to show less pronounced serrated flow and dynamic-strain-aging behavior under identical conditions.
The proposed explanation applies over 300–800 K and strain rates of 10^-4 to 10^-1 s^-1.
